text:
Samir: Heads-up, we keep hitting IP and ENI limits while provisioning the new Dedicated GPU pools (ap-northeast-1). Opening support ticket.
Leah: which limits exactly? EIP count / ENI attachments / secondary private IPs?
Samir: all of the above. Short summary: trying to bring up 3-AZ canary: 60 nodes/AZ (p4-class). Our early design used 4 public control IPs per node for control/ssh/monitoring. That was optimistic. Estimated peak EIP need ~720 + headroom.
Miguel: default EIP quota is 5 per account, so yeah we need support. Also watch ENI limits per instance type.
Samir: paste of the most common errors we've seen:
```
ERROR: AddressLimitExceeded: Your quota allows 5 Elastic IPs, requested 40
ERROR: RequestLimitExceeded: The maximum number of network interfaces for this instance type has been reached
```
Leah: do we have per-AZ breakdown for the support request? Support wants numbers per-AZ and justification for sustained vs burst.
Samir: here's what I'm going to submit as the first pass:
- Region: ap-northeast-1
- Purpose: Dedicated GPU fleet (canary -> prod) for enterprise customers requiring static egress for control-plane and whitelisting
- Nodes: 60 nodes/AZ * 3 AZs = 180 nodes
- Control static IPs: initially 2 per node reserved (bastion + metrics) = 360 EIPs
- Additional infra EIPs (LBs/jumpboxes/monitoring): 40
- Headroom: 25% -> total requested = 500 EIPs
- ENI attachments: request +1500 to accommodate primary+secondaries for pod IPs and observability interfaces
- VPC: request higher per-subnet assignable IPs (secondary private IPs)
- NAT/GW: request guidance and increased SNAT port availability or alternative recommended pattern
Miguel: that seems reasonable. Also include instance-type caps: for p4d.24xlarge max ENIs 50, for p4de.* lower, so detail expected mix and attachment plan.
ops-oncall: cost note: NAT Gateways scale costs quickly (hourly + processing). If we force all egress through NGW we'll pay significant monthly fees. Also SNAT port exhaustion is real with many small connections; consider carrier-grade NAT or pooling.
Leah: alternate proposal: reduce EIP count by moving most nodes behind NAT and only assigning static EIPs to control-plane/whitelist-critical flows. What's minimal static-IP set?
Samir: minimal control-plane static set: 1 per AZ for jumpbox + 1 per AZ for monitoring egress endpoint + customer-facing whitelists ~ 15 total -> super small. But customers asked for per-node fixed IPs for initial onboarding — that's the blocker.
Miguel: compromise: ask for 500 EIPs as temporary buffer and state migration plan to NAT+proxy within 6 months. AWS prefers to see a lifecycle/rollout plan.
Leah: good. I'll draft the ticket language with explicit growth timeline and include a network diagram and per-AZ expected sustained usage.
Samir: ticket created: AWS-INC-998112233. infra-bot attached the diagram. Status: awaiting AWS review.
infra-bot: Support ticket AWS-INC-998112233 created. Attachments: network-diagram-v1.svg, quota-growth-plan.pdf.
Leah: tagging @Miguel for ENI limits table and @ops-oncall for NAT cost estimation. Can both of you drop numbers within 12h?
Miguel: will post an ENI/IPv4-per-ENI table and suggested per-node private-IP allocation. Quick sample: p4d.24xlarge -> 8 usable secondaries planned; choose small per-pod IP use to avoid hitting per-subnet allocation.
ops-oncall: I'll run NAT/egress cost math. Quick rough: if 180 nodes average 30GB/day egress each, NGW data processing fees + hourly will be ~ $Xk/month. I'll give precise numbers. Also recommend a dedicated infra account for public IPs to centralize quota and billing.
Leah: decision for now: open support with 500 EIP ask + ENI + subnet IP increases, include migration plan to reduce EIPs over 3-6 months. If AWS pushes back, we fallback to NAT+whitelist and present that to customers. I'll own follow-ups.
Samir: thanks. I'll add the cost center and approval docs to the ticket.
Leah: updating: AWS acknowledged receipt, initial response says they need per-AZ exact numbers and confirmation we can accept a gradual quota increase. I'll post when they reply. :thumbsup:
